options.B: Using an unused VLAN as the native VLAN has no security benefit whatsoever and is done purely for cosmetic labeling reasons
options.C: An unused native VLAN automatically and completely disables 802.1Q tagging on the entire trunk, removing the need for any further configuration
options.D: Choosing an unused native VLAN is a mandatory requirement of the 802.1Q standard itself, with no flexibility to use any other VLAN as native

questions.explanation_es: Usar una VLAN dedicada sin uso real como VLAN nativa significa que, aunque un ataque de doble etiquetado quite la etiqueta externa, el frame termine efectivamente en una VLAN sin hosts reales, limitando el impacto práctico de ese tipo de ataque, y evita mezclar accidentalmente tráfico nativo sin etiquetar con una VLAN que realmente transporta tráfico de producción.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the relationship between a trunk link's configured 'allowed VLAN' list and the VLAN database (VLAN configuration) that must also exist on the switch?

options.A: A VLAN must generally exist in the switch's VLAN database before it can be meaningfully carried across a trunk's allowed-VLAN list; listing a VLAN as 'allowed' on a trunk does not itself create that VLAN if it was never configured/active on the switch
options.B: The allowed-VLAN list on a trunk automatically creates every listed VLAN in the switch's VLAN database, with no separate VLAN configuration step ever required
options.C: There is no relationship between the two; a trunk can carry any VLAN ID at all, whether or not that VLAN exists anywhere in the switch's configuration
options.D: The VLAN database and the trunk's allowed-VLAN list must always be configured with the exact same syntax on a completely separate, unrelated device

questions.explanation_es: Generalmente una VLAN debe existir en la base de datos VLAN del switch antes de que pueda transportarse de forma significativa a través de la lista de VLANs permitidas de un trunk; listar una VLAN como 'permitida' en un trunk no crea esa VLAN por sí sola si nunca se configuró/activó en el switch.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: How does VLAN pruning (whether manual via allowed-VLAN lists, or automatic via VTP pruning where supported) benefit STP and overall broadcast traffic on a trunk?

options.A: Restricting a trunk to only carry VLANs that are actually needed on the far end reduces unnecessary broadcast/multicast flooding and STP BPDU processing for VLANs that have no active devices on that particular link, improving efficiency and reducing unnecessary control-plane and data-plane overhead across the switched topology
options.B: VLAN pruning has no effect on broadcast traffic or STP processing whatsoever and exists purely as a documentation/labeling convenience
options.C: VLAN pruning always increases the total number of broadcast domains flooded across every trunk in the topology, the opposite of its intended effect
options.D: VLAN pruning can only be applied to Layer 3 routed links and has no applicability to Layer 2 trunk links

questions.explanation_es: Restringir un trunk para que solo transporte las VLANs realmente necesarias del otro lado reduce el flooding innecesario de broadcast/multicast y el procesamiento de BPDUs de STP para VLANs que no tienen dispositivos activos en ese enlace en particular, mejorando la eficiencia y reduciendo el overhead innecesario de plano de control y de datos en toda la topología conmutada.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: What is the effect of the 'switchport trunk pruning vlan' command, in environments where VTP pruning is used?

options.A: It restricts which VLANs are eligible to be automatically pruned by VTP pruning on that specific trunk, refining the default set of prunable VLANs rather than statically hardcoding the entire allowed-VLAN list the way 'switchport trunk allowed vlan' does
options.B: It has no relationship to VTP pruning at all and is used exclusively to configure the trunk's native VLAN
options.C: It permanently and unconditionally removes the listed VLANs from the switch's VLAN database entirely, deleting them
options.D: It is only relevant on Layer 3 routed interfaces and cannot be applied to a Layer 2 trunk port at all

questions.explanation_es: Restringe qué VLANs son elegibles para ser podadas automáticamente por VTP pruning en ese trunk específico, refinando el conjunto por defecto de VLANs podables, en lugar de fijar de forma estática toda la lista de VLANs permitidas como hace 'switchport trunk allowed vlan'.

questions.name: Trunking 802.1Q
questions.question: Why might a network engineer prefer to disable Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) entirely on end-user-facing access ports, even though those ports are not intended to become trunks?

options.A: Explicitly configuring access ports as 'switchport mode access' and disabling DTP negotiation on them closes off the possibility that a connected device attempting to speak DTP could ever trick the port into becoming a trunk, which is a defensive best practice regardless of whether an attack is actually anticipated on that specific port
options.B: DTP has no relevance to access ports whatsoever, since it is a protocol that only exists on Layer 3 interfaces, making this consideration moot
options.C: Disabling DTP on access ports is required before any VLAN can ever be assigned to that port, with the port otherwise remaining permanently unusable
options.D: DTP, if left enabled on an access port, automatically and immediately converts every connected end-user device into a Layer 3 router

questions.explanation_es: Configurar explícitamente los puertos de acceso como 'switchport mode access' y deshabilitar la negociación DTP en ellos cierra la posibilidad de que un dispositivo conectado que intente hablar DTP pueda engañar al puerto para que se vuelva trunk — una buena práctica defensiva independientemente de si se anticipa un ataque específico en ese puerto en particular.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What does the 'show etherchannel summary' command on a Cisco switch primarily help an administrator verify?

options.A: It shows the configured EtherChannel bundles, their protocol (LACP/PAgP/none), and the status of each member port (e.g., bundled 'P', suspended 's', individual 'I'), helping quickly identify whether all expected member links are actually bundled and forwarding as part of the channel
options.B: It displays only the physical color of the cables plugged into each EtherChannel member port, with no protocol or status information
options.C: It exclusively shows IP routing table entries and has no relationship to Layer 2 EtherChannel status at all
options.D: It can only be used to verify wireless access point associations and has no application to wired EtherChannel bundles

questions.explanation_es: Muestra los bundles de EtherChannel configurados, su protocolo (LACP/PAgP/ninguno), y el estado de cada puerto miembro (por ejemplo, bundled 'P', suspended 's', individual 'I'), ayudando a identificar rápidamente si todos los enlaces miembro esperados están realmente agrupados y reenviando como parte del canal.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What does it mean if a member port of an EtherChannel bundle shows a status of 'suspended' (commonly displayed as 's') in 'show etherchannel summary' output?

options.A: That port has been detected as mismatched in some way (e.g., inconsistent configuration compared to the other bundle members, such as speed/duplex/trunk settings), so it has been excluded from actively forwarding as part of the channel until the mismatch is resolved, even though it is still physically part of the configured bundle
options.B: A 'suspended' port is functioning perfectly normally and actively forwarding traffic exactly the same as a 'bundled' port, with the label being purely cosmetic
options.C: 'Suspended' means the port has been permanently and irreversibly removed from the switch's configuration entirely
options.D: 'Suspended' status only ever appears on ports that are physically unplugged, never due to any configuration mismatch

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto 'suspended' fue detectado con algún tipo de desajuste (por ejemplo, configuración inconsistente comparada con los demás miembros del bundle, como velocidad/duplex/ajustes de trunk), por lo que se excluyó de reenviar activamente como parte del canal hasta que se resuelva el desajuste, aunque siga siendo físicamente parte del bundle configurado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is it important that all member links of an EtherChannel bundle be configured with the exact same trunk 'allowed VLAN' list (when the bundle is used as a trunk)?

options.A: Because the bundle is treated as a single logical link, an inconsistent allowed-VLAN configuration across member ports could cause unpredictable behavior (such as certain VLANs being reachable only over some physical links and not others depending on the hashing algorithm's link selection), rather than the consistent, unified trunk behavior expected from a properly bundled EtherChannel
options.B: Allowed-VLAN consistency across member links has no actual effect on EtherChannel behavior and is purely a cosmetic documentation preference
options.C: EtherChannel automatically synchronizes and overrides each member port's allowed-VLAN list to match regardless of how each individual port was configured, making manual consistency unnecessary
options.D: Allowed-VLAN lists can only be configured on an entire EtherChannel port-channel interface and can never be configured on individual physical member ports in the first place

questions.explanation_es: Como el bundle se trata como un único enlace lógico, una configuración inconsistente de VLANs permitidas entre los puertos miembro podría causar comportamiento impredecible (por ejemplo, que ciertas VLANs solo sean alcanzables por algunos enlaces físicos y no por otros según el algoritmo de hashing), en lugar del comportamiento de trunk consistente y unificado esperado de un EtherChannel correctamente agrupado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is the general purpose of configuring a specific load-balancing hashing method (e.g., 'src-dst-ip' vs 'src-dst-mac') on an EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: The chosen hashing method determines which fields of a packet/frame are used as input to select which physical member link a given flow is placed on, and selecting a method that produces good entropy across many distinct flows (rather than always hashing to the same result) helps more evenly distribute traffic across all the bundle's physical links
options.B: The load-balancing hashing method controls exclusively how fast each individual physical link runs, unrelated to which link carries which flow
options.C: Load-balancing hashing methods only apply to wireless EtherChannel-like bundles and have no relevance to wired switch EtherChannel configuration
options.D: Configuring a hashing method is purely optional cosmetic labeling with zero effect on how traffic is actually distributed across the bundle's member links

questions.explanation_es: El método de hashing elegido determina qué campos de un paquete/frame se usan como entrada para seleccionar qué enlace físico miembro lleva un flujo determinado, y elegir un método que produzca buena entropía entre muchos flujos distintos (en vez de siempre hashear al mismo resultado) ayuda a distribuir el tráfico de forma más pareja entre todos los enlaces físicos del bundle.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why can EtherChannel load balancing sometimes appear 'unbalanced' even though the hashing algorithm is functioning correctly, particularly when there are relatively few distinct traffic flows?

options.A: With very few distinct flows (e.g., just two or three large flows), the hashing algorithm's output can happen to place multiple large flows onto the same physical link purely due to how the hash values distribute for that specific small set of flows, resulting in uneven utilization across the bundle even though the algorithm itself is working as designed — this is a statistical/flow-count limitation rather than a malfunction
options.B: EtherChannel load balancing is always perfectly even across every member link at every single moment in time, regardless of the number or size of active flows, making this scenario technically impossible
options.C: Unbalanced EtherChannel load distribution can only ever be caused by a hardware failure on one of the member ports, never by the number or characteristics of the actual traffic flows
options.D: Uneven load balancing indicates that LACP has failed entirely and none of the member links are actually part of the bundle any longer

questions.explanation_es: Con muy pocos flujos distintos (por ejemplo, solo dos o tres flujos grandes), el resultado del algoritmo de hashing puede coincidir en colocar varios flujos grandes en el mismo enlace físico simplemente por cómo se distribuyen los valores de hash para ese conjunto pequeño específico de flujos, resultando en utilización despareja del bundle aunque el algoritmo en sí funcione como fue diseñado — es una limitación estadística/de cantidad de flujos, no un mal funcionamiento.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is the relationship between an EtherChannel's logical 'Port-channel' interface and its physical member interfaces, in terms of Layer 3 configuration (for a routed EtherChannel)?

options.A: For a Layer 3 EtherChannel, IP addressing and most Layer 3 configuration is applied to the logical Port-channel interface itself, not to each individual physical member interface, since the member interfaces operate as part of the single logical bundled link represented by the Port-channel
options.B: Layer 3 IP addressing must always be configured identically and separately on every individual physical member interface, with no IP configuration ever applied to the logical Port-channel interface
options.C: A Layer 3 EtherChannel cannot have any IP address configured anywhere, on either the Port-channel interface or its members, under any circumstances
options.D: The logical Port-channel interface and its physical members must always be assigned to two entirely different, unrelated VRFs

questions.explanation_es: Para un EtherChannel de Capa 3, el direccionamiento IP y la mayor parte de la configuración de Capa 3 se aplica a la interfaz lógica Port-channel en sí, no a cada interfaz física miembro individualmente, ya que las interfaces miembro operan como parte del único enlace agrupado lógico representado por el Port-channel.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does STP typically treat a properly formed EtherChannel bundle in terms of the spanning-tree topology?

options.A: STP treats the entire EtherChannel bundle as a single logical link/port in its topology calculations, meaning it does not run a separate STP instance per physical member link; this avoids STP blocking individual member links (which would defeat the purpose of the bundle) while still allowing STP to block or forward the bundle as a whole relative to other paths in the topology
options.B: STP treats every physical member link of the bundle as a completely separate, independent port in its calculations, often blocking most of the member links individually and defeating the purpose of bundling them together
options.C: STP has no interaction with EtherChannel bundles whatsoever and is automatically and permanently disabled the moment any EtherChannel is configured anywhere on the switch
options.D: EtherChannel bundles can never participate in a spanning-tree topology at all and must always be manually excluded from STP calculations

questions.explanation_es: STP trata todo el bundle de EtherChannel como un único enlace/puerto lógico en sus cálculos de topología, es decir, no corre una instancia de STP separada por cada enlace físico miembro; esto evita que STP bloquee enlaces miembro individuales (lo cual anularía el propósito del bundle) mientras sigue permitiendo que STP bloquee o reenvíe el bundle como un todo respecto a otros caminos en la topología.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is 'Cross-Stack EtherChannel' (or similar multi-chassis EtherChannel technologies like StackWise or VSS-based EtherChannel), and what availability benefit does it provide over a standard single-switch EtherChannel?

options.A: It allows the individual physical member links of a single logical EtherChannel bundle to terminate on two (or more) physically separate switches that act as one logical switching entity, so that the failure of one entire physical chassis does not take down the whole EtherChannel bundle, only the member links that happened to terminate on the failed chassis
options.B: Cross-stack EtherChannel requires every member link to terminate on exactly the same single physical switch, with no cross-chassis capability of any kind, making the name purely misleading
options.C: Cross-stack EtherChannel eliminates the need for any physical cabling between the two switches involved in the bundle entirely
options.D: This technology is used exclusively for wireless access point redundancy and has no application to wired switch-to-switch EtherChannel links

questions.explanation_es: Permite que los enlaces físicos individuales miembro de un único bundle lógico de EtherChannel terminen en dos (o más) switches físicamente separados que actúan como una única entidad de switching lógica, de forma que la falla de un chasis físico completo no derribe todo el bundle de EtherChannel, solo los enlaces miembro que terminaban en el chasis que falló — una mejora de disponibilidad importante sobre un EtherChannel de un solo switch.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why must the member interfaces of an EtherChannel bundle generally be removed from any existing Layer 3 IP configuration before they can be added to a Layer 2 (switched) EtherChannel bundle?

options.A: A given physical interface cannot simultaneously have its own independent Layer 3 IP address configuration and also participate as a Layer 2 switched member of an EtherChannel bundle, since bundling a port into a Layer 2 channel converts that port's role into one governed by the logical Port-channel, not by any individually configured Layer 3 settings on that specific member port
options.B: There is no such requirement; a member port can retain a fully independent IP address and simultaneously participate in a Layer 2 EtherChannel bundle with no conflict whatsoever
options.C: EtherChannel bundling permanently and irreversibly deletes the physical interface from the switch's hardware inventory the moment it is added to a bundle
options.D: This requirement only applies to fiber-optic member interfaces and never to copper Ethernet member interfaces

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto físico dado no puede tener simultáneamente su propia configuración de dirección IP de Capa 3 independiente y participar como miembro conmutado de Capa 2 de un bundle de EtherChannel, ya que agrupar un puerto en un canal de Capa 2 convierte el rol de ese puerto en uno gobernado por el Port-channel lógico, no por ninguna configuración de Capa 3 configurada individualmente en ese puerto miembro específico.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What is a common recommended practice regarding the physical diversity of the individual links that make up an EtherChannel bundle, when availability is a priority?

options.A: Where practical, spreading member links across different physical line cards/modules (on a modular chassis) or different physical paths reduces the risk that a single hardware fault (like one line card failing) takes down every member link of the bundle simultaneously, preserving the redundancy benefit the bundle is meant to provide
options.B: Physical diversity of member links has no bearing on EtherChannel availability whatsoever, since all member links are logically treated identically regardless of which physical hardware they terminate on
options.C: Best practice explicitly recommends concentrating every member link of a bundle onto the exact same single physical line card specifically to simplify cabling, with availability being a secondary concern
options.D: EtherChannel technology itself physically prevents an administrator from ever placing member links on different line cards or modules

questions.explanation_es: Cuando es práctico, distribuir los enlaces miembro entre distintas tarjetas de línea/módulos físicos (en un chasis modular) o distintos caminos físicos reduce el riesgo de que una sola falla de hardware (como una tarjeta de línea cayéndose) derribe todos los enlaces miembro del bundle simultáneamente, preservando el beneficio de redundancia que el bundle está pensado para dar.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does LACP's 'system priority' and 'port priority' influence which links are actively used when more links are configured in a bundle than the maximum number of active links supported (e.g., more than 8)?

options.A: LACP uses these priority values (combined with system/port ID) to determine which links become the 'active' bundled members versus which are placed into a 'hot-standby' state, so that if an active member fails, one of the standby links can automatically take its place without requiring an administrator to manually reconfigure the bundle
options.B: System priority and port priority have no functional effect in LACP whatsoever and exist purely as unused legacy fields with no bearing on which links are active
options.C: These priority values are used exclusively to determine the color of the status LED on each member port, unrelated to which links actively forward traffic
options.D: LACP can never support more member links than the maximum number of simultaneously active links; any extra configured link is immediately and permanently rejected with no standby capability

questions.explanation_es: LACP usa estos valores de prioridad (combinados con el ID de sistema/puerto) para determinar qué enlaces se vuelven miembros activos del bundle versus cuáles quedan en estado de 'hot-standby', de forma que si un miembro activo falla, uno de los enlaces en espera pueda tomar su lugar automáticamente sin que un administrador tenga que reconfigurar manualmente el bundle.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is EtherChannel commonly used on the uplinks between an access-layer switch and a pair of redundant distribution-layer switches, in designs that support it (such as with a switch stack or VSS/StackWise at the distribution layer)?

options.A: EtherChannel across those uplinks combines the bandwidth of multiple physical links into one logical link while also providing redundancy, all without STP needing to block any of the redundant physical paths (since they appear as a single logical link to STP), which is more bandwidth-efficient than a design where STP simply blocks one of two separate redundant uplinks entirely
options.B: EtherChannel on access-to-distribution uplinks is used purely as a licensing requirement with no actual bandwidth or redundancy benefit
options.C: EtherChannel can only be used on downlinks toward end-user devices and is technically incompatible with switch-to-switch uplink connections
options.D: Using EtherChannel on these uplinks always reduces the total available bandwidth compared to leaving the links as separate, individually STP-managed ports

questions.explanation_es: El EtherChannel en esos uplinks combina el ancho de banda de varios enlaces físicos en un único enlace lógico mientras también provee redundancia, todo sin que STP necesite bloquear ninguno de los caminos físicos redundantes (ya que aparecen como un único enlace lógico ante STP), lo cual es más eficiente en ancho de banda que un diseño donde STP simplemente bloquea uno de dos uplinks redundantes por completo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What does the term 'min-links' configuration on an LACP EtherChannel bundle control?

options.A: It specifies the minimum number of member links that must be actively bundled and up for the entire Port-channel interface itself to be considered up; if the number of active links drops below that configured minimum, the whole logical Port-channel interface goes down, which can be used to ensure a minimum guaranteed bandwidth threshold is always met whenever the channel is considered operational
options.B: 'min-links' specifies the minimum physical cable length allowed for any member link in the bundle, measured in meters
options.C: 'min-links' has no functional purpose and is a deprecated, unused command with no effect on any current Cisco IOS platform
options.D: 'min-links' controls exclusively the minimum number of VLANs that must be allowed across the bundle's trunk configuration

questions.explanation_es: Especifica el número mínimo de enlaces miembro que deben estar activamente agrupados y up para que la propia interfaz Port-channel se considere up; si el número de enlaces activos cae por debajo de ese mínimo configurado, toda la interfaz Port-channel lógica cae, lo cual puede usarse para asegurar que siempre se cumpla un umbral mínimo de ancho de banda garantizado cuando el canal se considere operativo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is it generally recommended to configure EtherChannel member ports consistently for STP-related settings (such as PortFast, BPDU Guard) at the Port-channel interface level rather than trying to configure them differently per individual physical member port?

options.A: Because STP treats the bundle as a single logical port, STP-related settings are meant to apply to that logical Port-channel interface as a whole; attempting to configure conflicting STP settings on individual member ports could lead to inconsistent or unintended behavior, since STP does not actually process each member port as an independent, separately-controlled STP port
options.B: STP-related settings have no relevance to EtherChannel bundles at all and can be safely ignored entirely in any EtherChannel design
options.C: Each individual member port must always have a completely different, unique STP configuration from every other member port in the same bundle, or the bundle will refuse to form at all
options.D: PortFast and BPDU Guard can only ever be configured on access ports and can never be associated with any EtherChannel Port-channel interface under any circumstances

questions.explanation_es: Como STP trata el bundle como un único puerto lógico, los ajustes relacionados con STP están pensados para aplicarse a esa interfaz Port-channel lógica como un todo; intentar configurar ajustes de STP en conflicto en puertos miembro individuales podría llevar a comportamiento inconsistente o no deseado, ya que STP en realidad no procesa cada puerto miembro como un puerto STP independiente y controlado por separado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What common troubleshooting step should be taken if an EtherChannel bundle configured with LACP fails to form (all member ports remain individual/independent rather than bundled)?

options.A: Verify that both ends are running a compatible LACP mode combination (at least one side active, or active+passive), and that basic Layer 2 parameters (speed, duplex, trunk encapsulation/allowed VLANs, access VLAN if applicable) are consistent across all intended member ports on both switches, since a mismatch in any of these is a common cause of ports being suspended or failing to bundle
options.B: The only possible cause of an LACP bundle failing to form is a completely dead physical cable; no other configuration mismatch could ever prevent bundling
options.C: LACP bundles can never fail to form once configured; any apparent failure must actually be a display/reporting bug in the 'show etherchannel summary' command itself
options.D: The only fix for a failed LACP bundle is to physically replace every switch involved with new hardware

questions.explanation_es: Verificar que ambos extremos corran una combinación de modos LACP compatible (al menos un lado active, o active+passive), y que los parámetros básicos de Capa 2 (velocidad, duplex, encapsulación de trunk/VLANs permitidas, VLAN de acceso si aplica) sean consistentes en todos los puertos miembro pretendidos en ambos switches, ya que un desajuste en cualquiera de estos es una causa común de puertos suspendidos o que no logran agruparse.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: How does PAgP's 'desirable' and 'auto' negotiation modes compare conceptually to LACP's 'active' and 'passive' modes?

options.A: PAgP 'desirable' behaves similarly to LACP 'active' (it actively initiates negotiation), and PAgP 'auto' behaves similarly to LACP 'passive' (it only responds to negotiation initiated by the other side); as with LACP, two ports both set to the passive-equivalent mode (auto+auto) will not form a channel, since neither side initiates
options.B: PAgP and LACP negotiation modes are entirely unrelated concepts with no conceptual parallel between them whatsoever
options.C: PAgP 'desirable' and 'auto' are both equivalent to LACP 'active', meaning any combination of PAgP modes will always successfully negotiate a channel
options.D: PAgP has no negotiation modes at all and always forms a channel unconditionally regardless of any configuration on either side

questions.explanation_es: PAgP 'desirable' se comporta de forma similar a LACP 'active' (inicia activamente la negociación), y PAgP 'auto' se comporta de forma similar a LACP 'passive' (solo responde a una negociación iniciada por el otro lado); igual que con LACP, dos puertos configurados en el modo equivalente a pasivo (auto+auto) no formarán un canal, ya que ninguno de los dos inicia.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What advantage does LACP's ability to negotiate and dynamically detect a misconfigured or miswired member link provide, compared to a statically configured EtherChannel with no negotiation protocol ('mode on')?

options.A: With LACP, if a link is accidentally cabled to the wrong switch/port or otherwise doesn't match the expected bundle configuration, LACP's negotiation can detect the mismatch and keep that specific link out of the active bundle (avoiding it being blindly included), whereas a statically configured 'mode on' EtherChannel has no negotiation protocol running at all and will simply attempt to treat any physically connected, correctly-numbered member port as bundled, without any protocol-level verification that the far end agrees
options.B: Static 'mode on' EtherChannel configuration is always safer and more resilient to miscabling than LACP negotiation, the reverse of their actual behavior
options.C: LACP negotiation and static 'mode on' configuration provide functionally identical protection against miscabling, with no meaningful safety difference between them
options.D: LACP is incapable of detecting any form of link mismatch whatsoever and behaves identically to a statically configured channel in every respect

questions.explanation_es: Con LACP, si un enlace se cablea accidentalmente al switch/puerto equivocado o de algún modo no coincide con la configuración de bundle esperada, la negociación de LACP puede detectar el desajuste y mantener ese enlace específico fuera del bundle activo (evitando incluirlo ciegamente), mientras que un EtherChannel configurado estáticamente con 'mode on' no corre ningún protocolo de negociación e intentará simplemente tratar como agrupado a cualquier puerto miembro físicamente conectado y correctamente numerado, sin ninguna verificación a nivel de protocolo de que el otro extremo esté de acuerdo.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Why is using 'mode on' (static, unconditional EtherChannel with no negotiation protocol) generally discouraged in favor of LACP or PAgP negotiation, except in specific compatibility scenarios?

options.A: Because 'mode on' bypasses any negotiation entirely, both ends will unconditionally treat their configured ports as bundled even if there is a cabling mistake, a mismatched configuration, or the far end is not actually configured for a channel at all, which can silently cause a Layer 2 loop or other unexpected forwarding behavior that a negotiation protocol like LACP would have caught and prevented
options.B: 'mode on' configuration is objectively faster and more reliable in every single deployment scenario, with negotiation protocols like LACP offering no benefit over it whatsoever
options.C: 'mode on' cannot be configured on any modern Cisco switch platform and has been completely removed from current IOS software
options.D: There is no meaningful difference in risk between 'mode on' and LACP negotiation; the choice is purely a matter of personal preference with identical safety characteristics

questions.explanation_es: Como 'mode on' evita cualquier negociación por completo, ambos extremos tratarán sus puertos configurados como agrupados incondicionalmente aunque haya un error de cableado, una configuración desajustada, o el otro extremo ni siquiera esté configurado para un canal, lo cual puede causar silenciosamente un loop de Capa 2 u otro comportamiento de reenvío inesperado que un protocolo de negociación como LACP habría detectado y evitado.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: What happens to the traffic currently being carried by a specific member link of an active EtherChannel bundle if that individual physical link fails, while other member links remain up?

options.A: The EtherChannel protocol (LACP/PAgP) or the underlying hardware forwarding logic redistributes the flows that were using the failed link across the remaining active member links, typically resulting in a brief re-hash/re-convergence for the affected flows rather than a full outage of the entire logical channel, since the other member links continue forwarding traffic uninterrupted
options.B: The failure of any single member link, no matter how many other members remain active, always immediately takes down the entire logical Port-channel interface completely
options.C: Traffic that was using the failed member link is permanently lost and can never be recovered or redistributed to any other member link under any circumstances
options.D: EtherChannel bundles are physically incapable of continuing to operate with fewer member links than were originally configured, and require a full manual reconfiguration after any single link failure

questions.explanation_es: El protocolo de EtherChannel (LACP/PAgP) o la lógica de reenvío de hardware subyacente redistribuye los flujos que usaban el enlace caído entre los demás enlaces miembro activos, típicamente resultando en un breve re-hash/reconvergencia para los flujos afectados en lugar de una interrupción total del canal lógico, ya que los demás enlaces miembro siguen reenviando tráfico sin interrupción.

questions.name: EtherChannel
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes a limitation of relying on a hash-based load-balancing algorithm for EtherChannel, in terms of per-flow bandwidth?

options.A: Because the hashing algorithm places an entire flow onto a single physical member link (rather than splitting a single flow's packets across multiple links simultaneously), a single flow's maximum achievable throughput is generally limited to the bandwidth of one member link, not the combined bandwidth of the whole bundle, even if the bundle as a whole has much higher aggregate capacity
options.B: EtherChannel hashing always splits every individual flow's packets evenly across all member links simultaneously, guaranteeing that a single flow can achieve the full combined bandwidth of the entire bundle
options.C: Hash-based load balancing has no limitation whatsoever regarding per-flow throughput, and every flow always achieves the combined bandwidth of the entire bundle regardless of the hashing algorithm used
options.D: Per-flow bandwidth limitations only apply to wireless EtherChannel-like technologies and have no relevance to wired switch EtherChannel bundles

questions.explanation_es: Como el algoritmo de hashing coloca un flujo entero en un único enlace físico miembro (en lugar de dividir los paquetes de un mismo flujo entre varios enlaces simultáneamente), el rendimiento máximo alcanzable de un solo flujo generalmente está limitado al ancho de banda de un único enlace miembro, no al ancho de banda combinado de todo el bundle, aunque el bundle en su conjunto tenga una capacidad agregada mucho mayor — una limitación importante a tener en cuenta al diseñar para un solo flujo de alto ancho de banda.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How is the STP Root Bridge elected among a set of switches running standard 802.1D/RSTP Spanning Tree?

options.A: Each switch compares Bridge IDs (a combination of a configurable bridge priority and the switch's MAC address) received in BPDUs, and the switch with the numerically lowest Bridge ID is elected as the Root Bridge; a lower priority value wins, and the MAC address acts as a tiebreaker when priorities are equal
options.B: The Root Bridge is always the switch that was physically powered on most recently in the topology, regardless of any configured priority
options.C: The Root Bridge election is based exclusively on which switch has the highest number of physical ports, with priority and MAC address playing no role
options.D: Root Bridge election requires manual selection by an administrator typing a specific command on every single switch in the topology, with no automatic election process at all

questions.explanation_es: Cada switch compara los Bridge ID (una combinación de una prioridad de bridge configurable y la dirección MAC del switch) recibidos en BPDUs, y el switch con el Bridge ID numéricamente más bajo es elegido Root Bridge; un valor de prioridad más bajo gana, y la dirección MAC actúa como desempate cuando las prioridades son iguales.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Root Path Cost' in STP, and how does it influence which port on a non-root switch becomes the Root Port?

options.A: Root Path Cost is the cumulative cost of all links along the path from a given switch back to the Root Bridge, and each non-root switch selects, as its Root Port, the port with the lowest total Root Path Cost toward the Root Bridge, since that represents the best (lowest-cost) path back to the root
options.B: Root Path Cost is a fixed, unchangeable value that is always identical on every port of every switch in the topology, regardless of actual link speed or path length
options.C: Root Path Cost has no relationship to Root Port selection at all; the Root Port is chosen purely at random among all of a switch's active ports
options.D: Root Path Cost only applies to ports that are already blocking, and has no relevance to any port that is actively forwarding traffic

questions.explanation_es: El Root Path Cost es el costo acumulado de todos los enlaces a lo largo del camino desde un switch dado hasta el Root Bridge, y cada switch no-raíz selecciona, como su Root Port, el puerto con el menor Root Path Cost total hacia el Root Bridge, ya que representa el mejor camino (de menor costo) de regreso a la raíz.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is a 'Designated Port' in classic 802.1D Spanning Tree, and how is it selected on a given LAN segment?

options.A: For each LAN segment, the switch offering the lowest Root Path Cost to reach the Root Bridge through that segment has its port on that segment elected as the Designated Port, which is the port responsible for forwarding traffic onto and off of that particular segment (with Bridge ID as a tiebreaker for equal costs)
options.B: Every port on every switch in the topology is always a Designated Port simultaneously, with no distinction ever made between forwarding and blocking ports
options.C: A Designated Port is selected purely alphabetically based on the switch's configured hostname, with no relationship to path cost or Bridge ID at all
options.D: Designated Ports only exist on the Root Bridge itself; no other switch in the topology can ever have a Designated Port

questions.explanation_es: Para cada segmento de LAN, el switch que ofrece el menor Root Path Cost para llegar al Root Bridge a través de ese segmento tiene su puerto en ese segmento elegido como Designated Port, que es el puerto responsable de reenviar tráfico hacia y desde ese segmento en particular (con el Bridge ID como desempate en caso de costos iguales).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: In classic 802.1D STP, what are the five possible port states a port can transition through, and roughly what does each represent?

options.A: Blocking (not forwarding, only listening for BPDUs), Listening (preparing to forward, not yet learning MACs), Learning (building the MAC address table, still not forwarding user data), Forwarding (actively forwarding traffic), and Disabled (administratively shut down); a port typically moves through Blocking/Listening/Learning before reaching Forwarding, which is why classic 802.1D convergence can take tens of seconds
options.B: 802.1D STP has only two possible port states, 'On' and 'Off', with no intermediate states of any kind involved in convergence
options.C: The five port states are exclusively named after colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue, Purple) with no functional distinction between them
options.D: Every port state in 802.1D STP allows the port to immediately forward user data traffic with zero delay, making the concept of transitional states meaningless

questions.explanation_es: Blocking (no reenvía, solo escucha BPDUs), Listening (preparándose para reenviar, aún no aprende MACs), Learning (construyendo la tabla de direcciones MAC, todavía sin reenviar datos de usuario), Forwarding (reenviando tráfico activamente), y Disabled (apagado administrativamente); un puerto típicamente pasa por Blocking/Listening/Learning antes de llegar a Forwarding, por eso la convergencia del 802.1D clásico puede tardar decenas de segundos.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does RSTP's 'proposal/agreement' mechanism enable much faster convergence than classic 802.1D STP's timer-based transitions?

options.A: RSTP allows a switch to actively propose that its port become the new designated forwarding port and receive an explicit agreement back from its neighbor, enabling both sides to synchronize and move directly to forwarding without waiting through the fixed listening/learning timer delays that classic 802.1D relies on
options.B: RSTP's proposal/agreement mechanism has nothing to do with convergence speed and exists purely for logging/auditing purposes
options.C: RSTP achieves faster convergence exclusively by disabling all STP calculations entirely and simply forwarding on every port unconditionally with no loop prevention at all
options.D: The proposal/agreement mechanism only functions on the Root Bridge itself and has no effect on convergence anywhere else in the topology

questions.explanation_es: RSTP permite que un switch proponga activamente que su puerto se convierta en el nuevo puerto designado de reenvío y reciba un acuerdo explícito de su vecino, permitiendo que ambos lados se sincronicen y pasen directamente a forwarding sin esperar los retrasos de temporizador fijos de listening/learning en los que se basa el 802.1D clásico.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is a 'backup port' role, specific to RSTP, and when does it typically appear?

options.A: A backup port is a non-designated port role that appears when a switch has more than one port connected to the same shared LAN segment (e.g., via a hub), representing a redundant path to a segment the switch can already reach via its own designated port on that same segment; it is ready to take over the designated role if the current designated port on that segment fails
options.B: A backup port refers exclusively to a completely separate physical switch kept powered off in a storage closet as a spare replacement unit
options.C: Backup ports only exist in classic 802.1D STP and were entirely removed from RSTP, with no equivalent role present in RSTP
options.D: A backup port is simply another name for the Root Port, with the two terms being fully interchangeable

questions.explanation_es: Un puerto backup es un rol de puerto no designado que aparece cuando un switch tiene más de un puerto conectado al mismo segmento de LAN compartido (por ejemplo, vía un hub), representando un camino redundante hacia un segmento que el switch ya puede alcanzar por su propio puerto designado en ese mismo segmento; está listo para asumir el rol designado si el puerto designado actual de ese segmento falla.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What does 'BackboneFast' (a legacy Cisco STP enhancement) address, and why is it generally unnecessary once a network has migrated fully to RSTP?

options.A: BackboneFast reduced the time it took classic 802.1D STP to detect an indirect link failure (one not directly connected to the switch, discovered via the absence of expected BPDUs after the max-age timer), a scenario RSTP's more responsive BPDU-based mechanisms already handle quickly and natively without needing a separate feature
options.B: BackboneFast has no relationship to STP convergence at all and instead refers exclusively to a physical cable labeling scheme
options.C: BackboneFast is required in every RSTP deployment and cannot be omitted, contrary to being a legacy 802.1D-era enhancement
options.D: BackboneFast only affects Layer 3 routing convergence and has no relationship to Layer 2 Spanning Tree behavior whatsoever

questions.explanation_es: BackboneFast reducía el tiempo que le tomaba al 802.1D clásico detectar la falla de un enlace indirecto (uno no conectado directamente al switch, descubierto por la ausencia de las BPDUs esperadas tras el temporizador max-age), un escenario que los mecanismos más reactivos basados en BPDU de RSTP ya manejan rápida y nativamente sin necesitar una función separada.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does MST (Multiple Spanning Tree) group VLANs into 'MST instances' (MSTIs), and why does this grouping matter for scalability?

options.A: MST allows an administrator to map many VLANs onto a smaller number of MST instances, each running its own independent spanning-tree topology calculation; since the number of actual STP computations equals the (typically small) number of instances rather than the (potentially much larger) number of VLANs, this significantly reduces the CPU/control-plane load compared to running a fully separate STP instance for every single VLAN (as PVST+ does)
options.B: MST requires that every single VLAN always be mapped to its own unique, individual MST instance, providing no CPU savings whatsoever compared to PVST+
options.C: MST instances have no relationship to VLANs at all and are used exclusively to group physical switch ports by cable color
options.D: MST can only ever define a single instance total across the entire network, with no ability to run more than one spanning-tree topology anywhere

questions.explanation_es: MST permite que un administrador mapee muchas VLANs a una cantidad menor de instancias MST, cada una corriendo su propio cálculo de topología de spanning-tree independiente; como el número real de cálculos de STP es igual a la cantidad (típicamente pequeña) de instancias en lugar de la cantidad (potencialmente mucho mayor) de VLANs, esto reduce significativamente la carga de CPU/plano de control comparado con correr una instancia STP completamente separada por cada VLAN (como hace PVST+).

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What must be configured identically across all switches within the same MST 'region' for them to be considered part of that same region?

options.A: All switches in an MST region must share the same configured MST configuration name, revision number, and VLAN-to-instance mapping table; if any of these differ between two switches, they are considered to be in different MST regions, which affects how BPDUs and topology information are exchanged between them
options.B: Only the physical cable color connecting the switches needs to match; no software configuration parameters need to be consistent for switches to be considered part of the same MST region
options.C: MST regions are determined purely by the switches' physical geographic distance from each other, with no software configuration involved at all
options.D: Every switch in an MST region must have an identical hostname, with configuration name, revision, and VLAN mapping playing no role in region membership

questions.explanation_es: Todos los switches en una región MST deben compartir el mismo nombre de configuración MST, número de revisión, y tabla de mapeo VLAN-a-instancia; si alguno de estos difiere entre dos switches, se consideran en regiones MST distintas, lo cual afecta cómo se intercambian entre ellos las BPDUs y la información de topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does MST interact with switches running a different spanning-tree variant (like PVST+) at the boundary between an MST region and a non-MST switch?

options.A: MST includes interoperability behavior at region boundaries (using an Internal Spanning Tree/Common Spanning Tree, or CIST) so that MST regions can present a single, compatible spanning-tree view to neighboring switches running PVST+ or other STP variants, allowing the two to interoperate without requiring every single switch in the network to run the exact same STP variant
options.B: MST cannot interoperate with any other STP variant under any circumstances, requiring every single switch in an entire organization to be upgraded to MST simultaneously in one flash cut
options.C: MST regions automatically and permanently disable Spanning Tree entirely on every neighboring non-MST switch the moment they are connected
options.D: Boundary interoperability between MST and PVST+ requires manually disabling STP on the MST region entirely, defeating the purpose of running STP at all

questions.explanation_es: MST incluye comportamiento de interoperabilidad en los límites de región (usando un Internal Spanning Tree/Common Spanning Tree, o CIST) para que las regiones MST puedan presentar una vista de spanning-tree única y compatible a switches vecinos que corren PVST+ u otras variantes de STP, permitiendo que ambos interoperen sin requerir que absolutamente todos los switches de la red corran exactamente la misma variante de STP.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'UplinkFast' (a legacy Cisco 802.1D enhancement), and why is its function largely built into RSTP natively?

options.A: UplinkFast allowed an access-layer switch with a blocked backup uplink to quickly transition that backup link to forwarding if its active uplink failed, bypassing the normal listening/learning delay; RSTP achieves a similar (and generally faster/more general) rapid-failover capability natively through its alternate port role and proposal/agreement mechanism, without needing a separate legacy feature
options.B: UplinkFast has no relationship to uplink failover speed at all and refers exclusively to increasing the physical bandwidth of an uplink cable
options.C: UplinkFast is a mandatory feature that must be manually enabled even on switches already running RSTP, since RSTP does not provide any equivalent capability on its own
options.D: UplinkFast only applies to Layer 3 routed uplinks and has no relevance to Layer 2 STP-blocked redundant links

questions.explanation_es: UplinkFast permitía que un switch de capa de acceso con un uplink de respaldo bloqueado transicionara rápidamente ese enlace de respaldo a forwarding si su uplink activo fallaba, saltándose el retraso normal de listening/learning; RSTP logra una capacidad de conmutación rápida similar (y generalmente más rápida/general) de forma nativa a través de su rol de puerto alternate y el mecanismo de proposal/agreement, sin necesitar una función legacy separada.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is it generally recommended to manually set the STP root bridge priority (rather than relying on default priorities and letting the election happen arbitrarily) on the intended core/distribution switches in a campus design?

options.A: Manually and predictably setting a lower priority on the intended root switch(es) ensures the STP topology's root is a deliberately chosen, well-connected, high-capacity device rather than whichever switch happens to have the lowest default priority/MAC address, which could otherwise end up being an underpowered access-layer switch poorly suited to be the root of the topology
options.B: Manually setting root bridge priority has no actual effect on which switch becomes the root; the election always ignores configured priority and uses only the MAC address
options.C: Root bridge priority can only be configured on switches that are physically the very last ones added to the network, with no ability to configure it on any pre-existing switch
options.D: Setting root bridge priority manually is prohibited by the 802.1D and 802.1w standards and will cause the switch to reject the configuration

questions.explanation_es: Fijar de forma manual y predecible una prioridad más baja en el/los switch(es) destinado(s) a ser root asegura que la raíz de la topología STP sea un dispositivo deliberadamente elegido, bien conectado y de alta capacidad, en lugar de cualquier switch que resulte tener la prioridad/MAC más baja por defecto, lo cual de otro modo podría terminar siendo un switch de acceso de bajo poder poco adecuado para ser la raíz de la topología.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What specific risk does 'Root Guard' protect against that PortFast/BPDU Guard alone does not directly address?

options.A: Root Guard specifically prevents a port from ever becoming a Root Port by blocking any superior BPDU received on that port (rather than allowing that port's switch to become the new root), protecting the intended root switch's position in the topology; PortFast/BPDU Guard, by contrast, focuses on quickly enabling and protecting edge/access ports from receiving any BPDU at all, without specifically addressing root-role manipulation on non-edge ports
options.B: Root Guard and BPDU Guard provide functionally identical protection with no meaningful distinction between the two features
options.C: Root Guard's sole function is to physically prevent a cable from being unplugged from a designated root-facing port, with no relationship to BPDU processing at all
options.D: Root Guard only operates on the actual Root Bridge itself and has no effect when configured on any other switch in the topology

questions.explanation_es: Root Guard específicamente evita que un puerto se convierta en Root Port bloqueando cualquier BPDU superior recibida en ese puerto (en lugar de permitir que el switch de ese puerto se convierta en la nueva raíz), protegiendo la posición del switch raíz previsto en la topología; BPDU Guard, en cambio, se enfoca en habilitar rápidamente y proteger puertos de borde/acceso de recibir cualquier BPDU en absoluto, sin abordar específicamente la manipulación del rol de raíz en puertos que no son de borde.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What happens to a port protected by Root Guard if it receives a superior BPDU (one that would normally cause it to become a Root Port)?

options.A: The port is placed into a 'root-inconsistent' blocking state, preventing it from forwarding traffic (and from becoming the Root Port) as long as it continues receiving that superior BPDU; once the superior BPDUs stop being received, the port can automatically recover back to its normal STP-determined state
options.B: The port immediately and permanently becomes the new Root Port, exactly opposite to Root Guard's intended function
options.C: Root Guard has no defined behavior for this scenario and simply ignores any BPDU received, superior or not
options.D: The entire switch (not just the affected port) is immediately and permanently powered off the moment any superior BPDU is received anywhere on it

questions.explanation_es: El puerto se coloca en un estado de bloqueo 'root-inconsistent', impidiéndole reenviar tráfico (y convertirse en Root Port) mientras siga recibiendo esa BPDU superior; una vez que dejan de recibirse las BPDUs superiores, el puerto puede recuperarse automáticamente de vuelta a su estado normal determinado por STP.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is PortFast specifically intended only for ports connected to end hosts (like PCs, printers, or IP phones) and not for ports connecting to other switches?

options.A: PortFast causes a port to skip the normal listening/learning delay and transition immediately to forwarding, which is safe for a port that will never receive a BPDU from a downstream switch (an end host doesn't run STP); if PortFast were enabled on a port actually connecting to another switch, it could create a temporary Layer 2 loop before STP has a chance to properly detect the topology and block a redundant path
options.B: PortFast is actually intended exclusively for switch-to-switch trunk links and was never designed to be used on end-host-facing access ports at all
options.C: PortFast has no relationship to loop prevention or forwarding delay whatsoever, and is used purely to change the color of a port's status LED
options.D: PortFast can be safely enabled on any port type, including switch-to-switch links, with no additional risk of any kind

questions.explanation_es: PortFast hace que un puerto se salte el retraso normal de listening/learning y pase inmediatamente a forwarding, lo cual es seguro para un puerto que nunca recibirá una BPDU de un switch aguas abajo (un host final no corre STP); si PortFast se habilitara en un puerto que en realidad conecta a otro switch, podría crear un loop temporal de Capa 2 antes de que STP tenga la oportunidad de detectar correctamente la topología y bloquear un camino redundante — por eso PortFast siempre debe combinarse con BPDU Guard en puertos de acceso.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is the difference between BPDU Guard and BPDU Filter, both of which relate to how a port reacts to receiving a BPDU?

options.A: BPDU Guard, upon receiving any BPDU on a protected (typically PortFast) port, immediately puts that port into an err-disabled state to protect the topology, whereas BPDU Filter suppresses the sending and processing of BPDUs on that port entirely, which can be riskier since it silently prevents STP loop detection on that port rather than actively shutting it down when unexpected BPDUs appear
options.B: BPDU Guard and BPDU Filter are simply two different configuration command names for exactly the same underlying behavior, with no functional distinction whatsoever
options.C: BPDU Filter always shuts the port down completely upon receiving a BPDU, while BPDU Guard merely logs a warning message with no other action taken, the reverse of their actual typical behavior
options.D: Neither BPDU Guard nor BPDU Filter has any relationship to received BPDUs; both features instead control only the port's VLAN assignment

questions.explanation_es: BPDU Guard, al recibir cualquier BPDU en un puerto protegido (típicamente con PortFast), pone inmediatamente ese puerto en estado err-disabled para proteger la topología, mientras que BPDU Filter suprime el envío y procesamiento de BPDUs en ese puerto por completo, lo cual puede ser más riesgoso ya que silenciosamente impide la detección de loops de STP en ese puerto en lugar de apagarlo activamente cuando aparecen BPDUs inesperadas.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What is 'UDLD' (UniDirectional Link Detection), and what specific failure scenario does it address that basic STP BPDU exchange might not reliably catch?

options.A: UDLD detects a unidirectional link failure — where traffic can flow in one direction on a fiber pair (e.g., due to a crossed or damaged fiber strand) but not the other — a condition that can confuse STP (since BPDUs might still be received in one direction) and potentially lead to a forwarding loop; UDLD actively exchanges its own hello messages in both directions to verify true bidirectional connectivity and can err-disable a port if unidirectional behavior is detected
options.B: UDLD is used exclusively to measure the physical distance in meters of a fiber-optic cable, with no relationship to link directionality or loop prevention
options.C: UDLD and STP are functionally identical protocols that perform exactly the same detection and prevention function, making UDLD entirely redundant wherever STP is already running
options.D: UDLD only operates on copper Ethernet links and has no application whatsoever to fiber-optic connections, where unidirectional failures are most common

questions.explanation_es: UDLD detecta una falla de enlace unidireccional — donde el tráfico puede fluir en una dirección en un par de fibra (por ejemplo, por una hebra de fibra cruzada o dañada) pero no en la otra — una condición que puede confundir a STP (ya que las BPDUs podrían seguir recibiéndose en una dirección) y potencialmente llevar a un loop de reenvío; UDLD intercambia activamente sus propios mensajes hello en ambas direcciones para verificar conectividad bidireccional real y puede dejar el puerto err-disabled si detecta comportamiento unidireccional.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: How does 'err-disable recovery' functionality help operationally after a port has been automatically shut down by a protective feature like BPDU Guard or UDLD?

options.A: Err-disable recovery can be configured to automatically re-enable a port that was shut down due to a specific cause (like BPDU Guard or UDLD) after a configured timeout period, reducing the need for an administrator to manually intervene and re-enable the port every single time the protective feature triggers, while still preserving the initial protective shutdown behavior
options.B: Err-disable recovery permanently disables the affected port forever, with no possibility of it ever being automatically or manually re-enabled again under any circumstances
options.C: Err-disable recovery has no relationship to any protective feature like BPDU Guard or UDLD and instead controls only VLAN trunking negotiation timers
options.D: Enabling err-disable recovery completely disables the protective feature (BPDU Guard/UDLD) that caused the shutdown, preventing it from ever triggering again on that port

questions.explanation_es: La recuperación de err-disable puede configurarse para volver a habilitar automáticamente un puerto que fue apagado por una causa específica (como BPDU Guard o UDLD) después de un período de timeout configurado, reduciendo la necesidad de que un administrador intervenga manualmente y vuelva a habilitar el puerto cada vez que se dispara la función protectora, mientras sigue preservando el comportamiento inicial de apagado protectivo.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why might 'PVST+' (Per-VLAN Spanning Tree Plus) allow for more granular load balancing across redundant uplinks than a single common spanning-tree instance shared by all VLANs?

options.A: Because PVST+ runs a logically separate STP instance per VLAN, different VLANs can independently select different root bridges/root ports, allowing an administrator to intentionally make one uplink the forwarding path for some VLANs while a second redundant uplink forwards a different set of VLANs, spreading traffic across both physical uplinks rather than leaving one uplink completely blocked for every VLAN simultaneously
options.B: PVST+ always forces every single VLAN to use the exact same root bridge and identical forwarding topology, providing no additional load-balancing flexibility over a single shared STP instance
options.C: PVST+ has no relationship to load balancing whatsoever and exists purely to reduce the number of VLANs a switch can support
options.D: Load balancing across uplinks is only possible with EtherChannel and can never be achieved through any STP-based mechanism like PVST+

questions.explanation_es: Como PVST+ corre una instancia de STP lógicamente separada por VLAN, distintas VLANs pueden elegir de forma independiente distintos root bridges/root ports, permitiendo que un administrador haga intencionalmente que un uplink sea el camino de reenvío para algunas VLANs mientras un segundo uplink redundante reenvía un conjunto distinto de VLANs, repartiendo el tráfico entre ambos uplinks físicos en lugar de dejar un uplink completamente bloqueado para todas las VLANs simultáneamente.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: What operational cost does PVST+'s per-VLAN STP instance model impose as the number of VLANs on a switch grows very large, which MST was specifically designed to avoid?

options.A: Because PVST+ runs a fully separate STP computation and BPDU exchange for every single VLAN, a switch with hundreds of VLANs must perform hundreds of independent STP calculations and process a proportionally larger volume of BPDUs, consuming significantly more CPU and control-plane resources than MST's approach of mapping many VLANs onto a much smaller number of instances
options.B: PVST+ has no additional CPU or control-plane cost regardless of how many VLANs are configured, making MST's instance-mapping approach unnecessary from a scalability perspective
options.C: The number of VLANs configured on a switch has no relationship whatsoever to STP-related CPU utilization under PVST+
options.D: PVST+ automatically converts itself into MST once a switch exceeds a certain number of configured VLANs, with no administrator action required

questions.explanation_es: Como PVST+ corre un cálculo de STP y un intercambio de BPDUs completamente separado para cada VLAN, un switch con cientos de VLANs debe realizar cientos de cálculos de STP independientes y procesar un volumen proporcionalmente mayor de BPDUs, consumiendo significativamente más CPU y recursos de plano de control que el enfoque de MST de mapear muchas VLANs a una cantidad mucho menor de instancias — la razón principal detrás de la existencia de MST.

questions.name: STP/RSTP/MST, root guard, BPDU guard
questions.question: Why is it important that STP timers (hello time, forward delay, max age) be consistent with the actual diameter (maximum switch-to-switch hop count) of the switched topology?

options.A: The default STP timers are calculated assuming a certain maximum network diameter; if the actual topology's diameter exceeds what the configured timers were designed to safely accommodate, BPDUs might age out or convergence calculations might not have propagated fully across the entire topology in time, risking a temporary loop or slower-than-expected, potentially unreliable convergence behavior
options.B: STP timers have no relationship to network diameter whatsoever and can be set to any arbitrary value with zero risk regardless of how many switches are in the topology
options.C: Network diameter only matters for Layer 3 routing protocols like OSPF and has no bearing on Layer 2 Spanning Tree behavior of any kind
options.D: STP timers are automatically and dynamically recalculated in real time based on diameter with no default assumptions or administrator consideration ever required

questions.explanation_es: Los temporizadores por defecto de STP se calculan asumiendo un cierto diámetro máximo de red; si el diámetro real de la topología excede lo que esos temporizadores configurados fueron diseñados para acomodar de forma segura, las BPDUs podrían expirar o los cálculos de convergencia podrían no haberse propagado completamente por toda la topología a tiempo, arriesgando un loop temporal o un comportamiento de convergencia más lento de lo esperado y potencialmente poco confiable.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the role of the 'successor' route in EIGRP's DUAL algorithm?

options.A: The successor is the route with the lowest overall composite metric to a given destination, and it is the route that is actually installed in the routing table and used for forwarding, while a feasible successor (if one exists) is kept as a loop-free backup in the topology table
options.B: The successor is always a backup-only route that is never installed in the routing table under any circumstances
options.C: EIGRP does not use the term 'successor' at all; this terminology is exclusive to OSPF's SPF algorithm
options.D: A successor route is selected purely at random among all routes with an equal hop count, regardless of metric

questions.explanation_es: El successor es la ruta con el menor costo compuesto general hacia un destino dado, y es la ruta que realmente se instala en la tabla de enrutamiento y se usa para reenviar tráfico, mientras que un feasible successor (si existe) se mantiene como respaldo libre de loops en la tabla de topología.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the 'Feasibility Condition' that a backup route must satisfy in EIGRP to be considered a valid feasible successor (and thus be loop-free)?

options.A: A neighbor's advertised distance (its own reported metric to the destination) to that destination must be strictly less than the current successor's feasible distance (the local router's own best metric to that destination); this guarantees the neighbor is not routing back through the local router itself, avoiding a loop
options.B: The Feasibility Condition requires the backup route to have an identical metric to the successor route in every single case, with no tolerance for any difference
options.C: There is no such thing as a Feasibility Condition in EIGRP; any advertised route from any neighbor is automatically accepted as a feasible successor with no verification
options.D: The Feasibility Condition only applies to OSPF's SPF calculation and has no equivalent concept in EIGRP whatsoever

questions.explanation_es: La distancia anunciada de un vecino (su propio costo reportado hacia el destino) debe ser estrictamente menor que la distancia factible (feasible distance) actual del successor (el mejor costo propio del router local hacia ese destino); esto garantiza que el vecino no esté enrutando de vuelta a través del propio router local, evitando un loop.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How does EIGRP behave when a successor route fails and no feasible successor exists in the topology table for that destination?

options.A: EIGRP enters 'Active' state for that route and sends Query packets to its neighbors asking whether they have an alternate loop-free path to the destination, waiting for Reply packets before recalculating and re-installing a new best route (or declaring the destination unreachable if no neighbor has a valid path)
options.B: EIGRP immediately and permanently marks the entire routing process as failed and requires a full router reboot to recover from the loss of any single route
options.C: EIGRP always has a feasible successor pre-computed for every possible destination in every topology, making this active-state query scenario technically impossible
options.D: EIGRP silently drops all traffic to that destination forever with no attempt to query neighbors or recompute an alternate path of any kind

questions.explanation_es: EIGRP entra en estado 'Active' para esa ruta y envía paquetes Query a sus vecinos preguntando si tienen un camino alternativo libre de loops hacia el destino, esperando paquetes Reply antes de recalcular e instalar una nueva mejor ruta (o declarar el destino inalcanzable si ningún vecino tiene un camino válido).

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What potential problem does a prolonged EIGRP 'Stuck-In-Active' (SIA) condition represent, and what generally causes it?

options.A: An SIA condition occurs when a router does not receive Reply packets from one or more neighbors within the configured active-state timer after sending Query packets, often caused by a slow, congested, or unreachable neighbor that fails to reply in time; this can significantly delay convergence and, in the worst case, cause the router to reset the neighbor relationship with the non-responding neighbor
options.B: Stuck-In-Active is a normal, desirable steady-state condition that every EIGRP route is expected to remain in permanently under healthy network operation
options.C: SIA only occurs in OSPF, not EIGRP, and has no relationship to EIGRP's Query/Reply active-state process at all
options.D: An SIA condition is resolved automatically and instantly with zero impact on convergence time, regardless of how long a neighbor takes to reply

questions.explanation_es: Una condición SIA (Stuck-In-Active) ocurre cuando un router no recibe paquetes Reply de uno o más vecinos dentro del temporizador de estado activo configurado, a menudo causado por un vecino lento, congestionado o inalcanzable que no responde a tiempo; esto puede retrasar significativamente la convergencia y, en el peor caso, causar que el router reinicie la relación de vecindad con el vecino que no respondió.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What is the purpose of OSPF's SPF (Shortest Path First / Dijkstra) algorithm, run by every router within an area?

options.A: Each OSPF router uses SPF to independently calculate the shortest-cost tree from itself to every other router/network in its Link State Database, based on the complete topology information (link states) it has received, resulting in each router building its own view of the best path to every destination
options.B: SPF is calculated only once by a single centralized router for the entire OSPF domain, with every other router simply copying that one router's routing table verbatim with no independent calculation of their own
options.C: SPF has no relationship to path/cost calculation at all and is used exclusively to negotiate OSPF authentication passwords between neighbors
options.D: OSPF routers never run SPF; instead they rely entirely on distance-vector-style periodic full routing table exchanges, identical to RIP

questions.explanation_es: Cada router OSPF usa SPF para calcular de forma independiente el árbol de menor costo desde sí mismo hacia cada otro router/red en su base de datos de estado de enlace (LSDB), basándose en la información completa de topología (estados de enlace) que ha recibido, resultando en que cada router construya su propia vista del mejor camino hacia cada destino.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: Why does OSPF, as a link-state protocol, generally require every router within the same area to have an identical Link State Database (LSDB) before their individual SPF calculations produce a consistent, loop-free view of the topology?

options.A: Because SPF calculates each router's own shortest-path tree from the same underlying topology information, all routers within an area must have synchronized, identical LSDBs — if routers had inconsistent topology information, their independently calculated shortest-path trees could disagree and potentially create routing loops or blackholes
options.B: OSPF routers within the same area are permitted and expected to maintain completely different, unsynchronized LSDBs with no negative consequence to routing consistency
options.C: LSDB synchronization is only relevant across different OSPF areas and has no importance whatsoever for routers within the same single area
options.D: OSPF does not use an LSDB at all; that term is exclusive to EIGRP's topology table

questions.explanation_es: Como SPF calcula el árbol de menor camino de cada router a partir de la misma información de topología subyacente, todos los routers dentro de un área deben tener LSDBs sincronizadas e idénticas — si los routers tuvieran información de topología inconsistente, sus árboles de menor camino calculados independientemente podrían no coincidir y potencialmente crear loops de enrutamiento o agujeros negros.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: What distinguishes EIGRP as an 'advanced distance-vector' (sometimes called hybrid) protocol from a pure link-state protocol like OSPF, in terms of what information each router maintains?

options.A: EIGRP routers primarily learn about destinations and metrics reported by their directly connected neighbors (like a distance-vector protocol) rather than building a full topological map of the entire network the way OSPF's link-state LSDB does; EIGRP's DUAL algorithm and feasibility conditions add loop-avoidance sophistication beyond a classic distance-vector protocol like RIP, without requiring the full link-state topology database OSPF maintains
options.B: EIGRP and OSPF maintain functionally identical databases with no meaningful architectural distinction between a distance-vector and a link-state approach
options.C: EIGRP maintains a full link-state database identical in every respect to OSPF's LSDB, making the 'advanced distance-vector' label entirely inaccurate
options.D: EIGRP routers have no knowledge of metrics reported by neighbors at all and instead calculate every path using a link-state SPF algorithm identical to OSPF's

questions.explanation_es: Los routers EIGRP principalmente aprenden sobre destinos y métricas reportadas por sus vecinos directamente conectados (como un protocolo de vector distancia) en lugar de construir un mapa topológico completo de toda la red como hace la LSDB de estado de enlace de OSPF; el algoritmo DUAL de EIGRP y sus condiciones de factibilidad agregan sofisticación de prevención de loops más allá de un protocolo de vector distancia clásico como RIP, sin necesitar la base de datos de topología de estado de enlace completa que mantiene OSPF.

questions.name: EIGRP vs OSPF
questions.question: How do EIGRP and OSPF typically differ in how quickly they converge after a topology change, and why?

options.A: Both protocols are generally designed for fast convergence, but they achieve it differently: EIGRP can often converge almost instantly when a pre-computed feasible successor already exists (no recalculation needed), while OSPF must re-run SPF over its LSDB after a topology change is flooded, though modern OSPF implementations with incremental SPF and fast-hello/BFD tuning can also converge very quickly
options.B: EIGRP and OSPF are incapable of fast convergence under any circumstances and both always take several minutes at minimum to detect and react to any topology change
options.C: OSPF always converges instantly with zero computation required, while EIGRP always requires a full network-wide reboot to converge after any change
