options.A: IPv4 multicast addresses map to a MAC address in the range 01:00:5E:00:00:00 through 01:00:5E:7F:FF:FF, using only the lower 23 bits of the multicast IP address; since the IPv4 multicast address space uses 28 bits for group identification (after the fixed leading bits), this 23-bit mapping means multiple different multicast group addresses can map to the exact same destination MAC address, creating some theoretical ambiguity that receiving hosts must resolve at Layer 3
options.B: IPv4 multicast addresses always map one-to-one, uniquely and unambiguously, to a distinct Ethernet MAC address with absolutely no possibility of two different multicast IPs ever sharing the same destination MAC
options.C: Multicast IP-to-MAC mapping has no defined algorithm or standard whatsoever, and each vendor is free to implement a completely arbitrary, non-interoperable mapping
options.D: Multicast traffic is never actually transmitted using any Ethernet MAC address at all, relying instead exclusively on IP-layer forwarding with no Layer 2 addressing involved

questions.explanation_es: Las direcciones IPv4 multicast se mapean a una MAC en el rango 01:00:5E:00:00:00 a 01:00:5E:7F:FF:FF, usando solo los 23 bits inferiores de la dirección IP multicast; como el espacio de direcciones multicast IPv4 usa 28 bits para identificar el grupo (después de los bits iniciales fijos), este mapeo de 23 bits significa que múltiples direcciones de grupo multicast distintas pueden mapear a exactamente la misma MAC destino, creando cierta ambigüedad teórica que los hosts receptores deben resolver en Capa 3.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of IGMP snooping on a Layer 2 switch, and what problem does it solve compared to a switch with no IGMP awareness at all?

options.A: IGMP snooping allows a switch to inspect (snoop) IGMP membership messages passing through it, learning which specific switch ports have hosts that have actually joined a given multicast group, so it can forward multicast traffic for that group only out those specific ports rather than flooding all multicast traffic out every port in the VLAN (which is the default behavior without snooping, since multicast MAC addresses would otherwise be treated like unknown/broadcast traffic)
options.B: IGMP snooping has no relationship whatsoever to multicast traffic forwarding and instead only affects how VLAN trunking negotiation occurs between switches
options.C: Without IGMP snooping, a switch would be completely unable to forward any multicast traffic whatsoever to any port, rather than simply flooding it more broadly than necessary
options.D: IGMP snooping requires the switch to fully participate in Layer 3 PIM multicast routing, making it functionally identical to a full multicast router rather than a Layer 2 optimization feature

questions.explanation_es: El IGMP snooping le permite a un switch inspeccionar (espiar) los mensajes de membresía IGMP que pasan por él, aprendiendo qué puertos específicos del switch tienen hosts que realmente se unieron a un grupo multicast dado, para poder reenviar el tráfico multicast de ese grupo solo por esos puertos específicos en lugar de inundar todo el tráfico multicast por cada puerto de la VLAN (el comportamiento por defecto sin snooping, ya que las MAC multicast de otro modo se tratarían como tráfico desconocido/broadcast).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the difference between IGMPv1, IGMPv2, and IGMPv3, particularly regarding how a host can leave a multicast group?

options.A: IGMPv1 relies purely on membership reports timing out (a host that stops responding to periodic queries is eventually presumed to have left, which can be slow); IGMPv2 introduced an explicit 'Leave Group' message allowing a host to proactively signal it's leaving (speeding up group-leave convergence); IGMPv3 added support for source-specific membership reports (allowing a host to specify which particular sources it wants to receive multicast traffic from within a group, which SSM relies on)
options.B: IGMPv1, IGMPv2, and IGMPv3 are functionally and behaviorally completely identical in every respect, differing only in the version number field with no actual protocol enhancement between them
options.C: IGMPv3 removed the ability for a host to ever leave a multicast group at all, making group membership permanent and irrevocable once joined
options.D: IGMP versioning has no relationship whatsoever to how a host joins or leaves a group, and instead only affects the format of unrelated router hello messages

questions.explanation_es: IGMPv1 depende puramente de que los membership reports expiren (un host que deja de responder a las consultas periódicas eventualmente se asume que se fue, lo cual puede ser lento); IGMPv2 introdujo un mensaje explícito 'Leave Group' que le permite a un host señalar proactivamente que se está yendo (acelerando la convergencia de abandono de grupo); IGMPv3 agregó soporte para reportes de membresía específicos de fuente (permitiendo que un host especifique de qué fuentes en particular quiere recibir tráfico multicast dentro de un grupo, algo de lo que depende SSM).

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the role of the IGMP 'Querier' on a multicast-enabled subnet, and how is it typically elected?

options.A: The Querier is the router (or, in some Layer 2 IGMP snooping implementations, potentially a switch acting as a querier proxy) responsible for periodically sending IGMP membership query messages to solicit membership reports from hosts on that segment; when multiple routers are present on the same segment, the router with the lowest IP address is typically elected as the Querier
options.B: Every single router on a multicast-enabled segment always independently sends its own separate, uncoordinated IGMP queries with no concept of a single elected Querier role at all
options.C: The Querier role is fixed permanently to whichever router boots up last on the segment, with no relationship to IP addressing or any election process
options.D: IGMP Querier election is based on the highest IP address among the candidate routers, rather than the lowest

questions.explanation_es: El Querier es el router (o, en algunas implementaciones de IGMP snooping de Capa 2, potencialmente un switch actuando como proxy de querier) responsable de enviar periódicamente mensajes de consulta de membresía IGMP para solicitar reportes de membresía de los hosts en ese segmento; cuando hay múltiples routers en el mismo segmento, típicamente se elige como Querier al router con la IP más baja.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is a 'Rendezvous Point' (RP) in PIM Sparse Mode, and what happens if the RP for a given group becomes unreachable without any redundancy mechanism configured?

options.A: The RP acts as a meeting point where multicast sources register (informing the RP they have traffic to send) and where receivers initially join a shared distribution tree to start receiving that traffic; if the RP for a group becomes unreachable with no redundancy (like Anycast RP or MSDP) configured, new sources/receivers for that group generally cannot establish multicast delivery through the shared tree, disrupting multicast service for that group
options.B: The RP has no functional role whatsoever in PIM-SM and exists purely as an optional, non-functional configuration parameter with zero effect on multicast delivery
options.C: PIM Sparse Mode does not require or use any RP at all; this is a feature exclusive to PIM Dense Mode instead
options.D: If the RP becomes unreachable, PIM-SM automatically and instantly reroutes all traffic to use PIM Dense Mode flooding instead, with zero service disruption of any kind

questions.explanation_es: El RP actúa como un punto de encuentro donde las fuentes multicast se registran (informándole al RP que tienen tráfico para enviar) y donde los receptores inicialmente se unen a un árbol de distribución compartido para empezar a recibir ese tráfico; si el RP de un grupo se vuelve inalcanzable sin ningún mecanismo de redundancia configurado (como Anycast RP o MSDP), generalmente las fuentes/receptores nuevos de ese grupo no pueden establecer entrega multicast a través del árbol compartido, interrumpiendo el servicio multicast para ese grupo.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is 'Anycast RP', and how does it provide redundancy for the Rendezvous Point role in PIM Sparse Mode?

options.A: Anycast RP configures the same RP IP address on two or more physical routers, with those routers using MSDP (or a similar mechanism) between themselves to share source registration information, so that a source or receiver reaching whichever physically nearest RP-configured router (via normal IP routing to that shared anycast address) still gets full visibility of active sources across the redundant RPs, providing both load-sharing and failover redundancy for the RP function
options.B: Anycast RP requires configuring a completely different, unrelated IP address on every redundant RP router, with no shared address of any kind between them
options.C: Anycast RP has no relationship whatsoever to redundancy and instead refers exclusively to a method for compressing multicast packet headers to save bandwidth
options.D: Anycast RP can only ever be deployed with a single router acting as RP, making the term 'anycast' a misnomer with no actual multi-router redundancy capability

questions.explanation_es: Anycast RP configura la misma dirección IP de RP en dos o más routers físicos, y esos routers usan MSDP (u otro mecanismo similar) entre sí para compartir información de registro de fuentes, de forma que una fuente o receptor que llega a cualquiera de los routers configurados como RP físicamente más cercano (vía enrutamiento IP normal hacia esa dirección anycast compartida) igual obtenga visibilidad completa de las fuentes activas entre los RPs redundantes, dando tanto reparto de carga como redundancia de failover para la función de RP.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the difference between the 'shared tree' (RPT, rooted at the RP) and the 'shortest-path tree' (SPT, rooted at the actual source) in PIM Sparse Mode, and why might a receiver's last-hop router switch from one to the other?

options.A: Initially, a receiver joins the shared tree through the RP (a potentially suboptimal path, since traffic must first reach the RP before being forwarded to the receiver); PIM-SM includes a mechanism (SPT-switchover) that allows the last-hop router, once it learns the actual source's address, to switch to a source-rooted shortest-path tree directly to that source, which can provide a more optimal, lower-latency path once established
options.B: The shared tree and the shortest-path tree are simply two different names referring to the exact same single tree structure, with no actual distinction or switchover mechanism existing in PIM-SM
options.C: PIM Sparse Mode only ever uses a shortest-path tree and has no concept of a shared/RP-rooted tree at any point in its operation
options.D: Switching from the shared tree to the shortest-path tree always makes the path to the source strictly longer and less efficient, the reverse of the actual typical motivation for switching

questions.explanation_es: Inicialmente, un receptor se une al árbol compartido a través del RP (un camino potencialmente subóptimo, ya que el tráfico primero debe llegar al RP antes de reenviarse al receptor); PIM-SM incluye un mecanismo (SPT-switchover) que le permite al router del último salto, una vez que aprende la dirección de la fuente real, cambiar a un árbol de camino más corto enraizado en la fuente directamente, lo cual puede dar un camino más óptimo y de menor latencia una vez establecido.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What does PIM Source-Specific Multicast (SSM) require from the receiver (and IGMPv3) that fundamentally differs from the traditional PIM-SM shared-tree/any-source model?

options.A: In SSM, the receiver (via IGMPv3) explicitly specifies both the multicast group address AND the specific source address it wants to receive traffic from, allowing the last-hop router to build a source-rooted shortest-path tree directly to that specific, known source immediately, without needing an RP or a shared tree at all, since the receiver already knows exactly which source it wants
options.B: SSM requires a receiver to specify only the group address and explicitly forbids specifying any source address, the reverse of SSM's actual defining characteristic
options.C: SSM has no relationship whatsoever to IGMPv3 and instead relies exclusively on IGMPv1's simpler membership reporting mechanism
options.D: SSM eliminates the need for a source-rooted shortest-path tree entirely, relying purely and exclusively on a shared tree rooted at an RP, the opposite of its actual typical operation

questions.explanation_es: En SSM, el receptor (vía IGMPv3) especifica explícitamente tanto la dirección de grupo multicast COMO la dirección de fuente específica de la que quiere recibir tráfico, permitiendo que el router del último salto construya un árbol de camino más corto enraizado en la fuente directamente hacia esa fuente específica y conocida de inmediato, sin necesitar un RP ni un árbol compartido en absoluto, ya que el receptor ya sabe exactamente qué fuente quiere.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Why is PIM Dense Mode (PIM-DM) generally considered less scalable and less commonly deployed in modern enterprise networks compared to PIM Sparse Mode?

options.A: PIM-DM initially floods multicast traffic to every router in the domain (assuming receivers exist everywhere) and then relies on explicit prune messages from routers with no interested receivers to stop that flooding, which can waste bandwidth and processing resources across the network, especially in topologies where the actual set of interested receivers is a small subset of the total network, unlike PIM-SM's explicit-join model that only sends traffic where it's actually been requested
options.B: PIM-DM and PIM-SM are functionally and operationally identical protocols, with no meaningful scalability distinction between the two modes in any deployment scenario
options.C: PIM-DM requires significantly less bandwidth and fewer router resources than PIM-SM in every single deployment scenario, making it the generally preferred mode for large-scale networks, the opposite of the actual typical trade-off
options.D: PIM Dense Mode has been completely removed from all current Cisco IOS and IOS-XE software, making the comparison between the two modes purely historical with no relevance to any modern deployment

questions.explanation_es: PIM-DM inicialmente inunda el tráfico multicast a cada router del dominio (asumiendo que hay receptores en todos lados) y luego depende de mensajes explícitos de prune de los routers sin receptores interesados para detener esa inundación, lo cual puede desperdiciar ancho de banda y recursos de procesamiento en la red, especialmente en topologías donde el conjunto real de receptores interesados es un subconjunto pequeño de la red total, a diferencia del modelo de join explícito de PIM-SM que solo envía tráfico a donde realmente se solicitó.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What does the 'TTL threshold' or scope-based filtering technique (using the multicast packet's Time-To-Live value) historically help accomplish in a multicast deployment?

options.A: By configuring a router boundary to drop multicast packets whose TTL is below a certain threshold, an administrator can limit how far certain multicast traffic is allowed to propagate (for example, keeping a local test stream from ever leaving a specific site or campus), providing a simple, coarse-grained mechanism to scope multicast traffic distribution
options.B: TTL threshold filtering has no relationship whatsoever to limiting the propagation scope of multicast traffic and instead only affects unicast traffic's maximum hop count
options.C: Configuring a TTL threshold on a router boundary permanently and completely blocks all multicast traffic of every kind from crossing that boundary under any circumstances, regardless of the packet's actual TTL value
options.D: TTL threshold filtering can only be applied to IGMP control messages and has no effect whatsoever on actual multicast data traffic itself

questions.explanation_es: Configurando un límite en un router para descartar paquetes multicast cuyo TTL esté por debajo de cierto umbral, un administrador puede limitar hasta dónde se permite que se propague cierto tráfico multicast (por ejemplo, evitando que un stream de prueba local salga alguna vez de un sitio o campus específico), dando un mecanismo simple y de grano grueso para acotar la distribución del tráfico multicast.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Why is multicast commonly used for delivering IPTV/video broadcast streaming services to many simultaneous viewers, rather than using individual unicast streams to each viewer?

options.A: With multicast, the source only needs to send a single copy of the stream, and the network replicates that traffic only at points in the topology where it actually needs to branch toward multiple interested receivers, dramatically reducing the total bandwidth consumed on shared upstream links compared to sending a completely separate unicast copy of the same stream to every single individual viewer
options.B: Multicast requires sending a completely separate copy of the video stream to each viewer individually, providing no bandwidth efficiency benefit over unicast delivery, the reverse of multicast's actual defining advantage
options.C: Multicast can only ever support a maximum of exactly two simultaneous viewers for any given stream, making it unsuitable for any large-scale broadcast scenario
options.D: There is no meaningful bandwidth or scalability difference between multicast and unicast delivery for streaming video to many simultaneous viewers

questions.explanation_es: Con multicast, la fuente solo necesita enviar una única copia del stream, y la red replica ese tráfico solo en los puntos de la topología donde realmente necesita ramificarse hacia múltiples receptores interesados, reduciendo drásticamente el ancho de banda total consumido en los enlaces ascendentes compartidos comparado con enviar una copia unicast completamente separada del mismo stream a cada espectador individual.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'ip multicast-routing' global configuration command on a Cisco IOS router, and what happens if PIM is configured on an interface without this global command also being enabled?

options.A: 'ip multicast-routing' globally enables the router's multicast routing capability (creating multicast routing table structures and enabling the forwarding of multicast traffic between interfaces); without this global command enabled, PIM configured on individual interfaces generally will not actually route/forward multicast traffic between those interfaces, even though the interface-level PIM configuration itself may appear to be present
options.B: 'ip multicast-routing' only affects unicast routing table entries and has no relationship whatsoever to PIM or multicast traffic forwarding of any kind
options.C: PIM configured on an interface functions completely independently of the global 'ip multicast-routing' command, with full multicast forwarding capability regardless of whether that global command is present
options.D: 'ip multicast-routing' is a deprecated, non-functional legacy command that has no effect on any current Cisco IOS or IOS-XE release

questions.explanation_es: 'ip multicast-routing' habilita globalmente la capacidad de enrutamiento multicast del router (creando las estructuras de tabla de enrutamiento multicast y habilitando el reenvío de tráfico multicast entre interfaces); sin este comando global habilitado, PIM configurado en interfaces individuales generalmente no logrará realmente enrutar/reenviar tráfico multicast entre esas interfaces, aunque la configuración de PIM a nivel de interfaz en sí pueda parecer presente.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: Why does multicast traffic delivery generally rely on UDP rather than TCP as its Layer 4 transport?

options.A: TCP's connection-oriented, one-to-one acknowledgment/retransmission model is fundamentally difficult to reconcile with multicast's one-to-many delivery pattern (a source would need to individually track and manage separate acknowledgments/retransmissions with potentially thousands of receivers), so UDP's simpler, connectionless, best-effort delivery model is much better suited to how multicast actually needs to distribute traffic to many receivers simultaneously
options.B: Multicast traffic is always transported using TCP in every real-world deployment, with UDP playing no role whatsoever in multicast delivery
options.C: There is no meaningful architectural reason multicast tends to use UDP rather than TCP; the choice is purely an arbitrary historical convention with no actual technical justification
options.D: TCP is technically incapable of being used with any IP address at all, including unicast addresses, making its incompatibility with multicast unrelated to multicast's specific one-to-many delivery model

questions.explanation_es: El modelo de TCP orientado a conexión, con reconocimiento/retransmisión uno-a-uno, es fundamentalmente difícil de conciliar con el patrón de entrega uno-a-muchos de multicast (una fuente necesitaría rastrear y gestionar individualmente reconocimientos/retransmisiones separados con potencialmente miles de receptores), así que el modelo más simple, sin conexión y de mejor esfuerzo de UDP se adapta mucho mejor a cómo multicast realmente necesita distribuir tráfico a muchos receptores simultáneamente.

questions.name: Multicast
questions.question: What operational consideration is important when deploying multicast across a network that includes redundant Layer 3 paths, in terms of RPF (Reverse Path Forwarding) and routing table consistency?

options.A: Because RPF checks rely on the unicast (or MRIB-specific) routing table to determine the expected incoming interface for a given multicast source, inconsistent or asymmetric unicast routing (where the path used to reach a source differs from what the router's own routing table would suggest) can cause legitimate multicast traffic to fail the RPF check and be dropped, so multicast deployments generally benefit from having consistent, well-understood unicast routing to each active multicast source
options.B: RPF checks have no relationship whatsoever to the underlying unicast routing table and instead rely exclusively on a completely separate, independently maintained multicast-only physical network with no shared infrastructure with unicast routing at all
options.C: Redundant Layer 3 paths always improve multicast RPF check reliability with no possibility of ever causing a legitimate multicast packet to fail that check, regardless of any routing asymmetry
options.D: RPF checks are performed only once during initial router boot-up and are never re-evaluated afterward, regardless of any subsequent routing table changes

questions.explanation_es: Como las verificaciones RPF dependen de la tabla de enrutamiento unicast (o específica de MRIB) para determinar la interfaz de entrada esperada para una fuente multicast dada, un enrutamiento unicast inconsistente o asimétrico (donde el camino usado para alcanzar una fuente difiere de lo que sugeriría la propia tabla de enrutamiento del router) puede causar que tráfico multicast legítimo falle la verificación RPF y se descarte, así que los despliegues de multicast generalmente se benefician de tener un enrutamiento unicast consistente y bien entendido hacia cada fuente multicast activa.
